text:
Connor McMichael's first season in St. Louis has been a stop and start. The Blues put him on injured reserve on Nov. 24, he sat in New York, then he was back for Friday's win over Dallas, playing under 12 minutes. Eleven points in 23 games is a long way from the 46 he scored for Washington last season.

Most of the gap looks like bad luck, not a lost player. The Blues have scored 10.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the biggest shortfalls on our board, and he's shooting 9.4%. Those numbers usually swing back. St. Louis still controls 52% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him out there.

The real concern is in his own end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on last season (bottom 5% of forwards), and the Blues' expected-goal share with him is just under even. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the appeal: he carries the puck in on 56% of his entries and 60% of his shots come off the rush. Watch his minutes now that he's healthy.
